sentences.zh: 謝超宗

translations.literal: Xie Chaozong
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaozong

sentences.zh: 謝超宗，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Xie Chaozong was a native of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chaozong was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖靈運，宋臨川內史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingyun was Song grand administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingyun had been Song governor of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 父鳳，元嘉中坐靈運事，同徙嶺南，早卒。

translations.literal: His father Feng, in the Yuanjia era because of Lingyun's affair was exiled to Lingnan together with him and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father Feng, in the Yuanjia era was exiled to Lingnan with Lingyun and died young.

sentences.zh: 超宗元嘉末得還。

translations.literal: Chaozong was able to return at the end of Yuanjia.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong returned home at the end of the Yuanjia reign.

sentences.zh: 與慧休道人來往，好學，有文辭，盛得名譽。

translations.literal: He associated with the monk Huixiu, loved learning, had literary talent, and gained great renown.
translations.idiomatic: He kept company with the monk Huixiu, loved learning, wrote well, and won great renown.

sentences.zh: 解褐奉朝請。

translations.literal: He left coarse cloth as court gentleman attending audience.
translations.idiomatic: He left coarse cloth as a court gentleman attending audience.

sentences.zh: 新安王子鸞，孝武帝寵子，超宗以選補王國常侍。

translations.literal: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, the Xiaowu emperor's favored son — Chaozong by selection was made constant attendant in the princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ziluan of Xin'an, Emperor Xiaowu's favorite son, took Chaozong as constant attendant in his household.

sentences.zh: 王母殷淑儀卒，超宗作誄奏之，帝大嗟賞。

translations.literal: When the prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong composed a dirge and presented it; the emperor greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince's mother Lady Yin Shuyi died, Chaozong wrote a dirge and presented it; the emperor was deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 曰：「超宗殊有鳳毛，恐靈運復出。

translations.literal: He said: 「Chaozong truly has phoenix down — I fear Lingyun is born again.」
translations.idiomatic: He said: 「Chaozong truly has phoenix plumage — I fear Lingyun has been reborn.」

sentences.zh: 」轉新安王撫軍行參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred staff officer on the Pacification Army of the Prince of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was made staff officer on the Prince of Xin'an's Pacification Army.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，爲建安王司徒參軍事，尚書殿中郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Taishi he was staff officer to Prince Jian'an's secretariat, and director of the palace at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taishi he served Prince Jian'an's secretariat and was director of the palace at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，都令史駱宰議策秀才考格，五問竝得爲上，四、三爲中，二爲下，一不合與第。

translations.literal: In year three, bureau clerk Luo Zai deliberated the examination standard for recommending eminent scholars: in five questions all upper makes top grade, four or three middle, two lower, one failing earns no rank.
translations.idiomatic: In year three, bureau clerk Luo Zai proposed the examination standard for eminent scholars: five questions all top make highest grade, four or three middle, two lower, one fail earns no rank.

sentences.zh: 超宗議以爲「片辭折獄，寸言挫衆，魯史褒貶，孔《論》興替，皆無俟繁而後秉裁。

translations.literal: Chaozong argued: 「A phrase decides a case, a word defeats the crowd — the Lu historian's praise and blame, Confucius's Discourses on rise and fall, all need no prolixity before judgment is taken.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong argued: 「One phrase can decide a lawsuit, one word can overturn the crowd — the Lu historian's praise and blame, the Analects on rise and fall, need no prolixity before judgment.

sentences.zh: 夫表事之淵，析理之會，豈必委牘方切治道。

translations.literal: The depth of memorializing affairs and the meeting-point of analysis — must one always pile documents before the Way is touched?
translations.idiomatic: The depth of memorials and the crux of analysis — must one always heap documents before the Way is served?

sentences.zh: 非患對不盡問，患以恒文弗奇。

translations.literal: The worry is not incomplete answers but constant wording without marvel.
translations.idiomatic: The worry is not incomplete answers but flat phrasing without brilliance.

sentences.zh: 必使一通峻正，寧劣五通而常；

translations.literal: If one passage must be stern and correct, better five passes that are merely adequate;
translations.idiomatic: If one answer must be stern and correct, better five merely adequate passes;

sentences.zh: 與其俱奇，必使一亦宜採。

translations.literal: if all are marvelous, even one should be taken.」
translations.idiomatic: if all are brilliant, even one fine answer should count.」

sentences.zh: 」詔從宰議。

translations.literal: An edict followed Luo Zai's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed Luo Zai's proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒主簿，丹陽丞。

translations.literal: He was moved chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk of the secretariat and aide of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 建安王休仁引爲司徒記室，正員郎，兼尚書左丞中郎。

translations.literal: Prince Jian'an Xiuren took him as secretariat recorder, regular gentleman, and acting left director of the Secretariat among the gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian'an Xiuren made him secretariat recorder, regular gentleman, and acting left director among the secretariat gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以直言忤僕射劉康，左遷通直常侍。

translations.literal: Because blunt speech offended Vice Director Liu Kang, he was demoted regular attendant of unimpeded communication.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt speech offended Vice Director Liu Kang; he was demoted to regular attendant of unimpeded communication.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲領軍，數與超宗共屬文，愛其才翰。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor was Defender General they often composed texts together and he loved Chaozong's literary gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor was Defender General they often wrote together; he cherished Chaozong's talent.

sentences.zh: 衞將軍袁粲聞之，謂太祖曰：「超宗開亮迥悟，善可與語。

translations.literal: Defender General Yuan Can heard of it and told the founding emperor: 「Chaozong is open, bright, and far-seeing — pleasant to speak with.」
translations.idiomatic: Defender General Yuan Can heard and told the founding emperor: 「Chaozong is open, bright, and penetrating — good to talk with.」

sentences.zh: 」取爲長史、臨淮太守。

translations.literal: He was taken as chief clerk and grand administrator of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief clerk and governor of Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 粲旣誅，太祖以超宗爲義興太守。

translations.literal: When Can was executed the founding emperor made Chaozong grand administrator of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: After Can was executed the founding emperor made Chaozong governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: ，坐公事免。

translations.literal: , he was dismissed for a public-affairs offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for a public-affairs offense.

sentences.zh: 詣東府門自通，其日風寒慘厲，太祖謂四座曰：「此客至，使人不衣自暖矣。

translations.literal: He presented himself at the eastern mansion gate; that day the wind was bitterly cold; the founding emperor told the seated company: 「This guest's arrival makes one warm without putting on clothes.」
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself at the eastern mansion gate; the wind that day was bitterly cold; the founding emperor told the company: 「This guest arrives and one grows warm without dressing.」

sentences.zh: 」超宗旣坐，飲酒數甌，辭氣橫出，太祖對之甚歡。

translations.literal: Chaozong having sat, after several cups his words poured forth; the founding emperor was very pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Once seated, after several cups Chaozong's eloquence burst forth; the founding emperor delighted in him.

sentences.zh: 板爲驃騎諮議。

translations.literal: He was appointed by patent adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed by patent adviser to the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 及卽位，轉黃門郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor took the throne he was transferred gentleman of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended he was transferred to the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 有司奏撰立郊廟歌，敕司徒褚淵、侍中謝朏、散騎侍郎孔稚珪、太學博士王咺之、總明學士劉融、何法冏、何曇秀十人竝作，超宗辭獨見用。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized to compose suburban and temple hymns; the emperor ordered Chancellor Chu Yuan, attendant Xie Tiao, attendant at leisure Kong Zhigui, Erudite Wang Xuanzhi, Zongming scholars Liu Rong, He Fajiong, and He Yanxiu — ten in all — to compose; only Chaozong's hymn was used.
translations.idiomatic: Offices memorialized for suburban and temple hymns; the emperor ordered Chu Yuan, Xie Tiao, Kong Zhigui, Wang Xuanzhi, Liu Rong, He Fajiong, and He Yanxiu among ten to compose; only Chaozong's was adopted.

sentences.zh: 爲人仗才使酒，多所陵忽。

translations.literal: By nature he relied on talent and drank wine, and often slighted others.
translations.idiomatic: He relied on talent and wine and often slighted others.

sentences.zh: 在直省常醉，上召見，語及北方事，超宗曰：「虜動來二十年矣，佛出亦無如何！

translations.literal: In the direct-service offices he was often drunk; the emperor summoned him and spoke of northern affairs; Chaozong said: 「The barbarians have been stirring twenty years — even if the Buddha appeared, what could be done!」
translations.idiomatic: In the direct offices he was often drunk; summoned to discuss the north he said: 「The barbarians have stirred twenty years — even the Buddha could do nothing!」

sentences.zh: 」以失儀出爲南郡王中軍司馬。

translations.literal: For breach of decorum he was sent out as army supervisor of the Prince of Nanjun.
translations.idiomatic: For breach of decorum he was sent out as army supervisor to the Prince of Nanjun.

sentences.zh: 超宗怨望，謂人曰：「我今日政應爲司驢。

translations.literal: Chaozong resented it and told others: 「Today I ought rightly to be Director of Mules.」
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong resented it and said: 「Today I ought to be Director of Mules.」

sentences.zh: 」爲省司所奏，以怨望免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: The provincial office memorialized; for resentful speech he was dismissed and confined ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial office memorialized; for resentful speech he was dismissed and confined ten years.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚淵送湘州刺史王僧虔，閣道壞，墜水；

translations.literal: Chancellor Chu Yuan saw off Xiang governor Wang Sengqian; the gallery bridge broke and Yuan fell into the water;
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Chu Yuan saw off Xiang governor Wang Sengqian; the gallery bridge broke and Yuan fell into the water;

sentences.zh: 僕射王儉嘗牛驚，跣下車。

translations.literal: Vice Director Wang Jian once when his ox bolted leapt from the carriage barefoot.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Wang Jian's ox once bolted and he leapt from the carriage barefoot.

sentences.zh: 超宗撫掌笑戲曰：「落水三公，墮車僕射。

translations.literal: Chaozong clapped his hands in mockery: 「The third duke who fell in the water, the vice director who fell from his carriage.」
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong clapped and mocked: 「The third duke in the water, the vice director off his carriage.」

sentences.zh: 」前後言誚，稍布朝野。

translations.literal: Before and after, jests and sneers gradually spread through court and common.
translations.idiomatic: His jests and sneers gradually spread through court and town.

sentences.zh: 世祖卽位，使掌國史，除竟陵王征北諮議參軍，領記室。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne he was made to manage the national history, and made adviser to the Prince of Jingling's northern campaign with charge of the records office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended he managed the national history and was adviser on the Prince of Jingling's northern campaign with charge of the records office.

sentences.zh: 愈不得志。

translations.literal: He grew still more thwarted in his aims.
translations.idiomatic: He grew still more thwarted.

sentences.zh: 超宗娶張敬兒女爲子婦，上甚疑之。

translations.literal: Chaozong took Zhang Jing'er's daughter as his son's wife; the emperor was very suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong married his son to Zhang Jing'er's daughter; the emperor grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，敬兒誅，超宗謂丹陽尹李安民曰：「往年殺韓信，今年殺彭越，尹欲何計？

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, when Jing'er was executed, Chaozong told Danyang governor Li Anmin: 「Last year they killed Han Xin; this year Peng Yue — what plan does the governor intend?」
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year one, when Jing'er was executed, Chaozong told Li Anmin: 「Last year Han Xin; this year Peng Yue — what will you do, Governor?」

sentences.zh: 」安民具啓之。

translations.literal: Anmin reported it fully.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin reported everything.

sentences.zh: 上積懷超宗輕慢，使兼中丞袁彖奏曰：

translations.literal: The emperor's long resentment of Chaozong's insolence made him have acting censor Yuan Can memorialize, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's long resentment of Chaozong's insolence led acting censor Yuan Can to memorialize:

sentences.zh: :　　風聞征北諮議參軍謝超宗，根性浮險，率情躁薄。

translations.literal: It is heard that northern-campaign adviser Chaozong's root nature is floating and dangerous, his conduct rash and thin.
translations.idiomatic: It is reported that northern-campaign adviser Chaozong is by nature unstable and rash.

sentences.zh: 仕近聲權，務先諂狎。

translations.literal: In office he nears sounding power and is first to fawn and cozy up.
translations.idiomatic: Near sounding power he fawns and flatters first.

sentences.zh: 人裁疏黜，亟便詆賤。

translations.literal: When people barely slight him he at once slanders and despises them.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone barely slights him he slanders and despises them at once.

sentences.zh: 卒然面譽，旋而背毀。

translations.literal: Suddenly he praises to the face, then slanders behind the back.
translations.idiomatic: He flatters to one's face, then slanders behind one's back.

sentences.zh: 疑閒台賢，每窮詭舌。

translations.literal: He doubts and probes platform worthies, always exhausting crafty tongues.
translations.idiomatic: He probes court worthies with crafty tongues.

sentences.zh: 訕貶朝政，必聲凶言。

translations.literal: He mocks and belittles court government, always voicing vicious words.
translations.idiomatic: He mocks court government with vicious words.

sentences.zh: 腹誹口謗，莫此之甚；

translations.literal: Belly slander and mouth abuse — nothing surpasses this;
translations.idiomatic: Belly slander and open abuse — nothing surpasses this;

sentences.zh: 不敬不諱，罕與爲二。

translations.literal: irreverence and taboo-breaking — rarely a second.
translations.idiomatic: irreverence and breaking taboo — rarely a second.

sentences.zh: :　　輙攝白從王永先到臺辨問「超宗有何罪過，詣諸貴皆有不遜言語，竝依事列對」。

translations.literal: Your servant took clerk Wang Yongxian to the tribunal to examine what crimes Chaozong had — visiting the great all used insolent speech; let him answer item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant sent clerk Wang Yongxian to examine Chaozong's crimes — visits to the great all involved insolent speech; let him answer item by item.

sentences.zh: 永先列稱：「主人超宗恒行來詣諸貴要，每多觸忤，言語怨懟。

translations.literal: Yongxian listed: 「My master Chaozong constantly goes to visit the great; he often gives offense, speech resentful and raging.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian listed: 「My master constantly visits the powerful; he often offends them with resentful, raging speech.

sentences.zh: 與張敬兒周旋，許結姻好，自敬兒死後，惋歎忿慨。

translations.literal: He associated with Zhang Jing'er and promised a marriage alliance; after Jing'er died he sighed and raged in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He dealt with Zhang Jing'er and promised marriage; after Jing'er's death he raged in resentment.

sentences.zh: 今月初詣李安民，語論『張敬兒不應死』。

translations.literal: Early this month he visited Li Anmin and discussed that Zhang Jing'er ought not to have died.」
translations.idiomatic: Early this month he told Li Anmin that Zhang Jing'er ought not to have died.」

sentences.zh: 安民道『敬兒書疏，墨迹炳然，卿何忽作此語』？

translations.literal: Anmin said: 「Jing'er's letters and documents — the ink traces are clear — how can you suddenly speak thus?」
translations.idiomatic: Anmin said: 「Jing'er's letters — the evidence is clear — how can you say this?」

sentences.zh: 其中多有不遜之言，小人不悉盡羅縷諳憶。

translations.literal: Among them were many insolent words; a petty man cannot fully thread and remember them all.」
translations.idiomatic: There were many insolent words; a servant cannot recall them all.」

sentences.zh: 」如其辭列，則與風聞符同。

translations.literal: As his words list, they match what was heard.
translations.idiomatic: As listed, his words match the reports.

sentences.zh: 超宗罪自已彰，宜附常准。

translations.literal: Chaozong's crimes are already clear; he should follow the usual standard.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's guilt is clear; the usual standard should apply.

sentences.zh: :　　超宗少無行檢，長習民慝。

translations.literal: Chaozong in youth had no conduct; in age he learned the people's vices.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong in youth lacked conduct; in age he learned popular vices.

sentences.zh: 狂狡之迹，聯代所疾；

translations.literal: The traces of savage cunning — successive ages detested them;
translations.idiomatic: Savage cunning — ages detested it;

sentences.zh: 迷傲之釁，累朝點觸。

translations.literal: the fault of reckless pride — dynasties marked it.
translations.idiomatic: reckless pride — dynasties marked it.

sentences.zh: 剗容掃轍，久埋世表。

translations.literal: His countenance was swept from the road, long buried outside the world's lists.
translations.idiomatic: He was long cast from the world's rolls.

sentences.zh: 屬聖明廣愛，忍禍舒慈，捨之憲外，許以改過。

translations.literal: When the sage brightness broadly loved, bearing harm and showing mercy, he was spared beyond the statutes and allowed to reform.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage showed broad mercy he was spared beyond statute and allowed to reform.

sentences.zh: 野心不悛，在宥方驕；

translations.literal: His wild heart did not mend; within pardon he grew prouder;
translations.idiomatic: His wild heart did not mend; pardoned, he grew prouder;

sentences.zh: 才性無親，處恩彌戾。

translations.literal: talent and nature without kinship — in grace he grew more perverse.
translations.idiomatic: talented yet faithless — favored, he grew more perverse.

sentences.zh: 遂遘扇非端，空生怨懟，恣囂毒於京輔之門，揚凶悖於卿守之席。

translations.literal: He then fanned improper ends and bore resentment without cause, raging poison at the capital's gates and raising violence at a governor's seat.
translations.idiomatic: He fanned trouble and bore baseless resentment, raging at the capital's gates and violent at a governor's seat.

sentences.zh: 此而不翦，國章何寄？

translations.literal: If this is not cut down, to what does state law cling?
translations.idiomatic: If this is not cut down, what remains of state law?

sentences.zh: 此而可貸，孰不可容？

translations.literal: If this may be pardoned, what may not be borne?
translations.idiomatic: If this may be pardoned, what cannot?

sentences.zh: 請以見事免超宗所居官，解領記室。

translations.literal: Request that by the present affair he be removed from his posts and relieved of the records office.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that he be removed from office and relieved of the records office.

sentences.zh: 輙勒外收付廷尉法獄治罪。

translations.literal: Your servant urges he be seized outside and delivered to the tribunal for punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: We urge he be seized and delivered to the tribunal.

sentences.zh: 超宗品第未入簡奏，臣輙奉白簡以聞。

translations.literal: Chaozong's rank-grade has not entered the brief memorial; your servant ventures a white brief to report.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's rank has not entered the brief; your servant reports by white brief.

sentences.zh: 世祖雖可其奏，以彖言辭依違，大怒，使左丞王逡之奏曰：

translations.literal: The Shizu though he approved the memorial, because Can's words were evasive, was greatly angered and had left director Wang Junzhi memorialize:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu approved the memorial but, finding Can's wording evasive, was furious and had left director Wang Junzhi memorialize:

sentences.zh: :　　臣聞行父盡忠，無禮斯疾；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that a son honors his father with full loyalty — without ritual there is disease;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard: a son honors his father with full loyalty — without ritual there is rot;

sentences.zh: 農夫去草，見惡必耘。

translations.literal: the farmer uproots weeds — seeing evil he must hoe.
translations.idiomatic: the farmer uproots weeds — seeing evil he must root it out.

sentences.zh: 所以振纓稱良，登朝著績，未有尸位存私，而能保其榮名者也。

translations.literal: Therefore he who straightens his tassel is called good and who ascends court shows merit — never has one clung to office and hoarded private ends yet kept glory and name.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the upright are called good and those who serve court show merit — none cling to office for private ends and keep honor.

sentences.zh: :　　今月九日，治書侍御史臣司馬侃啓彈征北諮議參軍事謝超宗，稱「根性昏動，率心險放，悖議爽眞，囂辭犯實，親朋忍聞，衣冠掩目，輙收付廷尉法獄治罪」。

translations.literal: On the ninth of this month reviewing-secretary censor Sima Kan memorialized northern-campaign adviser Chaozong, saying his root nature is dull and rash, heart dangerous and unrestrained, rebellious discourse offends truth, arrogant words violate fact — kin and friends cannot bear to hear, caps and gowns cover their eyes — urge seizure and delivery to the tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth Sima Kan memorialized Chaozong: nature dull and rash, heart dangerous, arrogant speech violating fact — kin and friends cannot bear it — urge seizure for the tribunal.

sentences.zh: 處劾雖重，文辭簡略，事入主書，被却還外。

translations.literal: The impeachment though heavy, the wording brief; the matter entered the chief secretariat and was returned outside.
translations.idiomatic: The charge was heavy but wording brief; the chief secretariat returned it.

sentences.zh: 其晚，兼御史中丞臣袁彖改奏白簡，始粗詳備。

translations.literal: That evening acting censor Yuan Can revised the white brief, at last roughly complete.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Yuan Can revised the white brief into fuller form.

sentences.zh: 厥初隱衞，寔彖之由。

translations.literal: At first he hid and guarded — truly Can's doing.
translations.idiomatic: At first it was hidden — truly Can's doing.

sentences.zh: 尋超宗植性險戾，稟行凶詖，豺狼野心，久暴遐邇。

translations.literal: Chaozong's planted nature is dangerous and perverse, his endowed conduct vicious and false, wolf and jackal heart, long exposed near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's nature is dangerous, conduct vicious, wolf-heart long exposed to all.

sentences.zh: 張敬兒潛圖反噬，罰未塞諐，而稱怨痛枉，形于言貌。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing'er secretly plotted rebellion; punishment had not settled the guilt, yet he spoke of grievance and wrongful death, form on face and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing'er plotted rebellion; punishment had not settled all guilt, yet Chaozong spoke of wrongful death openly.

sentences.zh: 協附姦邪，疑閒勳烈，構扇異端，譏議時政，行路同忿，有心咸疾。

translations.literal: He cleaved to the wicked, doubted meritorious lieges, fanned heterodox ends, mocked the times — travelers shared anger, all who had heart were ill.
translations.idiomatic: He clung to villains, doubted meritorious men, mocked government — travelers were angry, the upright sickened.

sentences.zh: 而阿昧苟容，輕文略奏。

translations.literal: Yet Can fawned and tolerated, lightening text and thinning memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Can fawned and tolerated, thinning the memorial.

sentences.zh: 又彈事舊體，品第不簡，而釁戾殊常者，皆命議親奏，以彰深愆。

translations.literal: By old impeachment form, rank-grade is not briefed, but where guilt is extraordinarily violent, kin are ordered to memorialize to show deep fault.
translations.idiomatic: By old form rank is not briefed, but extraordinary guilt requires kin to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 況超宗罪愈四凶，過窮南竹，雖下輙收，而文止黃案，沈浮旡見，輕重相乖，此而不糾，憲綱將替。

translations.literal: Chaozong's crime exceeds the Four Evils and surpasses the Nanzhu cases — though seizure was ordered, the text stopped at the yellow dossier; float and sink unseen, light and heavy at odds — if this is not corrected, law's net will fail.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong's crime exceeds the Four Evils — though seizure was ordered, the memorial stopped at the yellow dossier; if uncorrected, law's net fails.

sentences.zh: :　　彖才識疏淺，質幹無聞，憑戚昇榮，因慈荷任。

translations.literal: Can's talent and insight are shallow, substance and stem unheard-of; by in-law he rose, by mercy he bore office.
translations.idiomatic: Can's talent is shallow, substance unknown; by marriage he rose, by mercy he held office.

sentences.zh: 不能克己厲情，少酬恩獎，撓法容非，用申私惠。

translations.literal: He could not restrain himself and steel his feelings, scarcely repaying grace; he bent law to harbor wrong and show private favor.
translations.idiomatic: He could not restrain himself or repay grace; he bent law for private favor.

sentences.zh: 何以糾正邦違，式明王度？

translations.literal: How rectify the state's violations and display the king's measure?
translations.idiomatic: How can he rectify violations and display royal measure?

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，請以見事免彖所居官，解兼御史中丞，輙攝曹依舊下禁止視事如故。

translations.literal: Your servants deliberating request that by the present affair Can be removed, relieved of acting censor, and your servant take charge to forbid him yet view affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: We ask Can be removed and relieved of acting censor, forbidden yet to view affairs as before.

sentences.zh: :　　治書侍御史臣司馬侃雖承稟有由，而初無疑執，亦合及咎。

translations.literal: Reviewing-secretary censor Sima Kan though he followed orders had at first no doubtful hold — he too should share guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Kan though following orders had no firm hold at first — he too shares guilt.

sentences.zh: 請杖督五十，奪勞百日。

translations.literal: Request staff beating fifty and deprivation of merit a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: Request fifty strokes and deprivation of merit for a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 令史卑微，不足申盡，啓可奉行。

translations.literal: Clerks are lowly — insufficient to declare fully — the memorial may be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks are lowly — the memorial may be carried out.

sentences.zh: :　　侃奏彈之始，臣等竝卽經見加推糾，案入主書，方被却檢，疏謬之諐，伏追震悚。

translations.literal: At the start of Kan's impeachment your servants at once saw and pressed; the case entered the chief secretariat and was returned for inspection — the fault of looseness and error fills us with dread.
translations.idiomatic: At Kan's first memorial we pressed at once; the chief secretariat returned it — we are filled with dread at the looseness.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「超宗釁同大逆，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: The edict said: 「Chaozong's guilt equals great treason; crime cannot bear pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said: 「Chaozong's guilt equals great treason; the crime cannot be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 彖匿情欺國，愛朋罔主，事合極法，特原收治，免官如案，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: Can hid facts and deceived the state, loving faction and misleading the ruler — the affair fits extreme law; specially pardoned to seizure and treatment; removal as memorialized, confinement ten years.」
translations.idiomatic: Can hid facts and deceived the state — the affair fits extreme law; specially pardoned to seizure; removal as memorialized, confinement ten years.」

sentences.zh: 」超宗下廷尉，一宿髮白皓首。

translations.literal: Chaozong was sent down to the tribunal; in one night his hair turned white.
translations.idiomatic: Chaozong was sent to the tribunal; in one night his hair turned white.

sentences.zh: 詔徙越州，行至豫章，上敕豫章內史虞悰曰：「謝超宗令於彼賜自盡，勿傷其形骸。」

translations.literal: An edict exiled him to Yue; reaching Zhang commandery the emperor edicted Zhang interior governor Yu Cong: 「Order Chaozong to take his own life there — do not harm his body.」
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Yue; at Zhang commandery the emperor edicted Yu Cong: 「Have Chaozong kill himself there — do not harm his body.」

sentences.zh: 明年，超宗門生王永先又告超宗子才卿死罪二十餘條。

translations.literal: The next year Chaozong's student Wang Yongxian again reported Chaozong's son Caiqing for more than twenty capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The next year his student Wang Yongxian reported his son Caiqing for more than twenty capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 上疑其虛妄，以才卿付廷尉辯，以不實見原。

translations.literal: The emperor doubted the falsehood; Caiqing was given to the tribunal and cleared as untrue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor doubted the charges; Caiqing was tried and cleared.

sentences.zh: 永先於獄自盡。

translations.literal: Yongxian killed himself in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian killed himself in prison.

sentences.zh: 劉祥

translations.literal: Liu Xiang
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang

sentences.zh: 劉祥字顯徵，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang, styled Xianzheng, was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang, styled Xianzheng, was a man of Ju in Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 祖式之，吳郡太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shizhi was grand administrator of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shizhi had been governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 父敳，太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: His father Ao was attendant gentleman of the Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ao had been attendant gentleman of the Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 祥宋世解褐爲巴陵王征西行參軍，歷驃騎中軍二府，太祖太尉東閣祭酒，驃騎主簿。

translations.literal: In Song times Xiang left coarse cloth as western-campaign staff officer to the Prince of Baling, served both central and rapid-cavalry staffs, eastern-pavilion sacrifice officer to the founding emperor as Grand Mentor, and chief clerk to the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he was western-campaign staff officer to the Prince of Baling, served both central and rapid-cavalry staffs, sacrifice officer to the founding emperor as Grand Mentor, and rapid-cavalry chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 建元中，爲冠軍征虜功曹，爲府主武陵王曅所遇。

translations.literal: In the Jianyuan era he was merit officer on the champion general's barbarian-pacification staff and was favored by his lord Prince Zhao of Wuling Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyuan he was merit officer on the champion's barbarian-pacification staff and was favored by Prince Zhao of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 除正員外。

translations.literal: He was made regular outside gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was made regular outside gentleman.

sentences.zh: 祥少好文學，性韻剛疏，輕言肆行，不避高下。

translations.literal: Xiang in youth loved literature; his nature was stiff and loose; he spoke lightly and acted freely, not avoiding high or low.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang in youth loved literature; he was stiff and unrestrained, speaking and acting freely without regard for rank.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚淵入朝，以腰扇鄣日，祥從側過，曰：「作如此舉止，羞面見人，扇鄣何益？

translations.literal: Chancellor Chu Yuan entered court shading the sun with a waist fan; Xiang passed by the side and said: 「Making such gestures — ashamed to show your face to people — what good is shading?」
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yuan entered court fanning the sun; Xiang passed and said: 「Gestures like that — ashamed to show your face — what good is the fan?」

sentences.zh: 」淵曰：「寒士不遜。

translations.literal: Yuan said: 「The cold scholar is not deferential.」
translations.idiomatic: Yuan said: 「The poor scholar lacks deference.」

sentences.zh: 」祥曰：「不能殺袁、劉，安得免寒士？

translations.literal: Xiang said: 「Unable to kill Yuan and Liu — how can you escape being a cold scholar?」
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: 「You could not kill Yuan Can and Liu — how are you not a cold scholar?」

sentences.zh: 」永明初，遷長沙王鎮軍，板諮議參軍，撰《宋書》，譏斥禪代，尚書令王儉密以啓聞，上銜而不問。

translations.literal: At the start of Yongming he was moved to the Prince of Changsha's Pacification Army as adviser and compiled the Song History, mocking the abdication; Director Wang Jian secretly reported; the emperor harbored resentment but did not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongming he advised the Prince of Changsha's Pacification Army and compiled the Song History, mocking the abdication; Wang Jian secretly reported; the emperor resented but did not pursue it.

sentences.zh: 歷鄱陽王征虜，豫章王大司馬諮議，臨川王驃騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: He served the Prince of Poyang's barbarian-pacification staff, the Prince of Yuzhang's Grand Marshal staff, and the Prince of Linchuan's Rapid Cavalry attendant gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Prince of Poyang, the Prince of Yuzhang's Grand Marshal staff, and the Prince of Linchuan's Rapid Cavalry as attendant gentleman.

sentences.zh: 祥兄整爲廣州，卒官，祥就整妻求還資，事聞朝廷。

translations.literal: Xiang's elder brother Zheng was in Guangzhou and died in office; Xiang demanded return of assets from Zheng's wife; the matter reached court.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zheng died as Guangzhou governor; Xiang demanded Zheng's wife return assets; the matter reached court.

sentences.zh: 於朝士多所貶忽。

translations.literal: Toward court gentlemen he was much deprecating and slighting.
translations.idiomatic: He slighted many court gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 王奐爲僕射，祥與奐子融同載，行至中堂，見路人驅驢，祥曰：「驢！

translations.literal: Wang Huan was vice director; Xiang rode with Huan's son Rong; reaching the middle hall they saw a passerby driving a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan was vice director; Xiang rode with Huan's son Rong; in the middle hall they saw a man driving a donkey.

sentences.zh: 汝好爲之，如汝人才，皆已令僕。

translations.literal: Xiang said: 「Donkey! You do well to do this — men of talent like you are already all made servants.」
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said: 「Donkey! Keep at it — men of your talent are already all servants.」

sentences.zh: 」著《連珠》十五首以寄其懷。

translations.literal: He composed fifteen Linked Pearls to lodge his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He composed fifteen Linked Pearls to voice his feelings.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：

translations.literal: The text says:
translations.idiomatic: The text says:

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞興教之道，無尚必同；

translations.literal: It is said that the way to raise teaching has nothing loftier than sameness;
translations.idiomatic: It is said the way to raise teaching has nothing loftier than unity;

sentences.zh: 拯俗之方，理貴袪弊。

translations.literal: the method to save custom — principle honors removing harm.
translations.idiomatic: the method to save custom honors removing harm.

sentences.zh: 故揖讓之禮，行乎堯舜之朝；

translations.literal: Therefore the rites of yielding were practiced in Yao and Shun's court;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore yielding was practiced in Yao and Shun's court;

sentences.zh: 干戈之功，盛於殷周之世。

translations.literal: the merit of weapons flourished in the Yin and Zhou age.
translations.idiomatic: the merit of arms flourished in Yin and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 清風以長物成春，素霜以凋嚴戒節。

translations.literal: Pure wind forms spring through long things; white frost sets stern warning through withering.
translations.idiomatic: Pure wind makes spring through growth; white frost warns through decay.

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞鼓鼖懷音，待揚桴以振響；

translations.literal: It is said drums hoard sound and await the raised frame to ring; heaven and earth hold spirit and rely on dark and bright to set posts.
translations.idiomatic: It is said drums hoard sound awaiting the frame's strike; heaven and earth hold spirit and rely on light and dark to set posts.

sentences.zh: 天地涵靈，資昏明以垂位。

translations.literal: Therefore worthy assistants rose by Tang and Wu;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore worthy ministers rose through Tang and Wu;

sentences.zh: 是以俊乂之臣，借湯、武而隆；

translations.literal: brilliant rulers governed borrowing Yi and Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: brilliant rulers governed through Yi and Zhou.

sentences.zh: 英達之君，假伊、周而治。

translations.literal: It is said when hunger hangs over the year one envies coarse herb satiety;
translations.idiomatic: It is said when hunger hangs over the year one envies coarse herbs;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞懸饑在歲，式羨藜藿之飽；

translations.literal: when heavy heat burns the body one does not think of fox-fur warmth.
translations.idiomatic: when heat burns the body one forgets fox-fur warmth.

sentences.zh: 重炎灼體，不念狐白之溫。

translations.literal: Therefore talent is splendid when it meets the age;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore talent shines when it meets the age;

sentences.zh: 故才以偶時爲劭；

translations.literal: the Way is honored when it tunes custom.
translations.idiomatic: the Way is honored when it tunes custom.

sentences.zh: 道以調俗爲尊。

translations.literal: It is said the skill of habituated numbers borrows things to seek;
translations.idiomatic: It is said practiced skill borrows tools to advance;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞習數之功，假物可尋；

translations.literal: the brightness of exploration follows the age and lacks.
translations.idiomatic: the brightness of inquiry follows the age and fails.

sentences.zh: 探索之明，循時則缺。

translations.literal: Therefore the builder goes daily and the cord-and-ink craft does not decay;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the builder works daily and measure does not decay;

sentences.zh: 故班匠日往，繩墨之伎不衰；

translations.literal: the great Way ever exists yet the wit of the moving spirit is forever cut.
translations.idiomatic: the great Way endures yet moving spirit's wit is cut off.

sentences.zh: 大道常存，機神之智永絕。

translations.literal: It is said principle fixed in the heart needs no vulgar praise;
translations.idiomatic: It is said principle fixed in the heart needs no vulgar praise;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞理定於心，不期俗賞；

translations.literal: feeling threaded through the age has no grief for worldly insult.
translations.idiomatic: feeling threaded through the age need not grieve worldly insult.

sentences.zh: 情貫於時，無悲世辱。

translations.literal: Therefore each fragrance has its nature — no need for Miluo's grief;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore each nature has its fragrance — no need for Qu Yuan's grief;

sentences.zh: 故芬芳各性，不待汨渚之哀；

translations.literal: brightness as treasure needs no the Chu south's weeping.
translations.idiomatic: brightness as treasure needs no Chu mourner's weeping.

sentences.zh: 明白爲寶，無假荊南之哭。

translations.literal: It is said on a terrace of a hundred ren no frost-defying tree stands;
translations.idiomatic: It is said on a hundred-ren terrace no frost-proof tree stands;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞百仞之臺，不挺陵霜之木；

translations.literal: in a spring of a foot night-glory gems sometimes fall.
translations.idiomatic: in a foot-deep spring night gems sometimes fall.

sentences.zh: 盈尺之泉，時降夜光之寶。

translations.literal: Therefore principle may be great yet oppose expedient;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore principle may be great yet oppose expedient measure;

sentences.zh: 故理有大而乖權；

translations.literal: things may be slight yet reach the Way.
translations.idiomatic: things may be slight yet touch the Way.

sentences.zh: 物有微而至道。

translations.literal: It is said loyal ministers rush to integrity — not necessarily in court;
translations.idiomatic: It is said loyal ministers rush to integrity — not only in court;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞忠臣赴節，不必在朝；

translations.literal: arrayed knights right the age — righteousness stored then acts.
translations.idiomatic: knights right the age — when righteousness is stored they act.

sentences.zh: 列士匡時，義存則幹。

translations.literal: Therefore Shen Baoxu wept and bore no meat-eating plot;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Shen Baoxu wept and bore no plot of comfort;

sentences.zh: 故包胥垂涕，不荷肉食之謀；

translations.literal: Wang Ao threw himself away and did not master hall-and-altar reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ao gave his life and did not master court reckoning.

sentences.zh: 王歜投身，不主廟堂之算。

translations.literal: It is said wisdom beyond the body — principle cannot be trapped;
translations.idiomatic: It is said wisdom beyond the body — principle cannot trap it;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞智出乎身，理無或困；

translations.literal: sound tied to things — talent has its limit.
translations.idiomatic: sound tied to things — talent has limits.

sentences.zh: 聲係於物，才有必窮。

translations.literal: Therefore wings that cross waves cannot calm them;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore wave-crossing wings cannot calm the sea;

sentences.zh: 故陵波之羽，不能淨浪；

translations.literal: trees that fill peaks cannot stop wind.
translations.idiomatic: trees that fill peaks cannot stop the wind.

sentences.zh: 盈岫之木，無以輟風。

translations.literal: It is said fine treasure meeting bluntness — then marvel-text does not show;
translations.idiomatic: It is said fine treasure meeting bluntness — marvel-text does not show;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞良寶遇拙，則奇文不顯；

translations.literal: reached scholar meeting slander — then heroic talent's glory is quenched.
translations.idiomatic: reached scholar meeting slander — heroic talent's glory is quenched.

sentences.zh: 達士逢讒，則英才滅耀。

translations.literal: Therefore fallen leaves shade and the bright moon is barred;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore fallen leaves cast shade and the bright moon is dimmed;

sentences.zh: 故墜葉垂蔭，明月爲之隔輝；

translations.literal: hall and eaves keep light — the orchid lamp sometimes does not shine.
translations.idiomatic: the hall keeps light — the orchid lamp sometimes does not shine.

sentences.zh: 堂宇留光，蘭燈有時不照。

translations.literal: It is said traces admiring the near square — necessarily momentum is lost to far greatness;
translations.idiomatic: It is said clinging to the near — momentum is lost to the far;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞迹慕近方，必勢遺於遠大；

translations.literal: feeling tied to rushing — solid principle is forgotten in fat retirement.
translations.idiomatic: feeling tied to rushing — principle is forgotten in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 情係驅馳，固理忘於肥遯。

translations.literal: Therefore men by the river sometimes knot the net of envy;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore riverside men sometimes knot nets of envy;

sentences.zh: 是以臨川之士，時結羨網之悲；

translations.literal: porters at the stall do not embrace the dragon-slayer's sigh.
translations.idiomatic: market porters do not sigh like dragon-slayers.

sentences.zh: 負肆之氓，不抱屠龍之歎。

translations.literal: It is said what numbers divide — though near it is hard;
translations.idiomatic: It is said what numbers divide is hard though near;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞數之所隔，雖近則難；

translations.literal: what feeling matches — though far it is easy.
translations.idiomatic: what feeling matches is easy though far.

sentences.zh: 情之所符，雖遠則易。

translations.literal: Therefore climbing and sighing at flowing frost sometimes wins heaven-moved sincerity;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore sighing at frost sometimes wins heaven-moved sincerity;

sentences.zh: 是以陟歎流霜，時獲感天之誠；

translations.literal: weeping blood following punishment yet no wisdom to awaken the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: weeping blood under punishment yet no wit to awaken the ruler.

sentences.zh: 泣血從刑，而無悟主之智。

translations.literal: It is said wonder exhausted in knowing — spirit far then abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: It is said wonder ends in knowing — spirit far is abandoned;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞妙盡於識，神遠則遺；

translations.literal: merit touching men — feeling slight then shown.
translations.idiomatic: merit touching men — slight feeling then shows.

sentences.zh: 功接於人，情微則著。

translations.literal: Therefore bells and drums in the hall — ten thousand men incline ear;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore bells in the hall — ten thousand men listen;

sentences.zh: 故鍾鼓在堂，萬夫傾耳；

translations.literal: the great Way dwelling in the body — sometimes not met.
translations.idiomatic: the great Way in the body — sometimes not met.

sentences.zh: 大道居身，有時不遇。

translations.literal: It is said grass arrayed in deep peaks does not alter last winter's wither;
translations.idiomatic: It is said grass in deep peaks keeps last winter's wither;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞列草深岫，不改先冬之悴；

translations.literal: pine planted in stream bottoms has not the late frost's glory stolen.
translations.idiomatic: pine in stream beds keeps late frost's unbroken glory.

sentences.zh: 植松澗底，無奪後凋之榮。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhan Qin thrice removed yet without lowest-fool praise;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Zhan Qin thrice removed without lowest-fool praise;

sentences.zh: 故展禽三黜，而無下愚之譽；

translations.literal: a thousand autumns one season — yet without highest-wit's fame.
translations.idiomatic: a thousand years one season — yet without highest wit's fame.

sentences.zh: 千秋一時，而無上智之聲。

translations.literal: It is said rare-age treasure — against the time then cheap;
translations.idiomatic: It is said rare treasure is cheap against the time;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞希世之寶，違時則賤；

translations.literal: marvelous custom's vessel — without a sage must sink.
translations.idiomatic: marvelous vessels sink without a sage.

sentences.zh: 偉俗之器，無聖必淪。

translations.literal: Therefore sounding jade was dismissed from Chu peaks, ceremonial cap exhausted among Yue men.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore sounding jade was dismissed from Chu peaks, caps failed among Yue men.

sentences.zh: 故鳴玉黜於楚岫，章甫窮於越人。

translations.literal: It is said hearing ended in deafness — not the surging sound's grasp;
translations.idiomatic: It is said hearing ended in deafness — not surging sound's grasp;

sentences.zh: :　　蓋聞聽絕於聦，非疾響所握；

translations.literal: spirit closed in blindness — not overflowing light's illumination.
translations.idiomatic: spirit closed in blindness — not overflowing light's shine.

sentences.zh: 神閉於明，非盈光所燭。

translations.literal: Therefore mountain-breaking thunder does not start the deaf man's ear;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore mountain thunder does not wake the deaf;

sentences.zh: 故破山之雷，不發聾夫之耳；

translations.literal: bright night's glow does not open the blind elder's eye.
translations.idiomatic: bright night's glow does not open the blind man's eyes.

sentences.zh: 朗夜之輝，不開矇叟之目。

translations.literal: Someone presented Xiang's Linked Pearls to the emperor; the emperor ordered acting censor Ren Xia to memorialize:
translations.idiomatic: Someone presented Xiang's Linked Pearls; the emperor ordered Ren Xia to memorialize:

sentences.zh: 有以祥《連珠》啓上者，上令御史中丞任遐奏曰：「祥少而狡異，長不悛徙，請謁絕於私館，反脣彰於公庭，輕議乘輿，歷貶朝望，肆醜無避，縱言自若。

translations.literal: 「Xiang from youth was cunning and strange, in age unrepentant; visits ended at private lodges, back talk showed in public halls; lightly discussing the imperial carriage, repeatedly deprecating court hope; venting ugliness without avoidance, letting words run as they would.
translations.idiomatic: 「Xiang from youth was cunning and strange, in age unrepentant; private visits, public back talk; he slighted the throne and mocked court figures without restraint.

sentences.zh: 厥兄浮櫬，天倫無一日之悲，南金弗獲，嫂姪致其輕絕，孤舟敻反，存沒相捐，遂令暴客掠奪骸柩，行路流歎，有識傷心。

translations.literal: His elder brother floated the coffin — one day of human kinship without grief; southern gold not obtained — sister-in-law and nephew met his light severance; lone boat far returned — living and dead abandoned each other — thus violent guests plundered the coffin; travelers sighed; the knowing were wounded.
translations.idiomatic: His brother's coffin floated — no kin grief; he fought his sister-in-law for goods; living and dead abandoned — robbers plundered the coffin; travelers sighed, the knowing were wounded.

sentences.zh: 攝祥門生孫狼兒列『祥頃來飲酒無度，言語闌逸，道說朝廷，亦有不遜之語，實不避左右，非可稱紙墨。

translations.literal: Your servant took Xiang's student Sun Lang'er's list: 「Xiang of late drinks without limit, words reckless and excessive, speaks of court — also insolent words, truly not avoiding bystanders, not fit for paper and ink.」
translations.idiomatic: Student Sun Lang'er listed: 「Xiang drinks without limit, speech reckless, discusses court with insolent words, not fit for record.」

sentences.zh: 兄整先爲廣州，於職喪亡，去年啓求迎喪，還至大雷，聞祥與整妻孟爭計財物瞋忿，祥仍委前還，後未至鵲頭，其夜遭劫，內人竝爲凶人所淫略』。

translations.literal: Elder brother Zheng was first in Guangzhou and died in office; last year he memorialized to bring the coffin; returning to Dalei he heard Xiang and Zheng's wife Meng contending over goods in rage; Xiang then left the coffin and did not come; later he did not reach Que'tou — that night met robbery and inner people were all violated by villains.」
translations.idiomatic: Brother Zheng died in Guangzhou; Xiang fought Zheng's wife Meng over goods, abandoned the coffin, and later met robbery where household members were violated.」

sentences.zh: 如所列與風聞符同。

translations.literal: As listed it matches what was heard.
translations.idiomatic: As listed it matches reports.

sentences.zh: 請免官付廷尉。」

translations.literal: Request removal from office and delivery to the tribunal.」
translations.idiomatic: Request removal and delivery to the tribunal.」

sentences.zh: 上別遣敕祥曰：「卿素無行檢，朝野所悉。

translations.literal: The emperor separately edicted Xiang:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor separately edicted Xiang:

sentences.zh: 輕棄骨肉，侮蔑兄嫂，此是卿家行不足，乃無關他人。

translations.literal: 「You from of old had no conduct — known to court and common.
translations.idiomatic: 「You have long lacked conduct — known to all.

sentences.zh: 卿才識所知，蓋何足論。

translations.literal: Lightly abandoning flesh and bone, insulting elder brother's wife — this is your family's insufficient conduct, not others' affair.
translations.idiomatic: You abandoned kin and insulted your sister-in-law — your family's failing, not others' affair.

sentences.zh: 位涉清途，於分非屈。

translations.literal: The talent and insight you know — how is it worth discussion?
translations.idiomatic: The talent you possess — how is it worth discussion?

sentences.zh: 何意輕肆口噦，詆目朝士，造席立言，必以貶裁爲口實。

translations.literal: Your rank touched the clear path — in allotment not bent.
translations.idiomatic: Your rank touched the clear path — not bent in allotment.

sentences.zh: 冀卿年齒已大，能自感厲，日望悛革。

translations.literal: Why lightly vent your mouth and sneer at court gentlemen, making seats and standing speech — must depreciation be the mouth's substance?
translations.idiomatic: Why vent your mouth and sneer at court gentlemen, always deprecating as habit?

sentences.zh: 如此所聞，轉更增甚，諠議朝廷，不避尊賤，肆口極辭，彰暴物聽。

translations.literal: I hoped your years were already great and you could reform yourself; day by day I looked for repentance.
translations.idiomatic: I hoped age would make you reform; I looked for repentance daily.

sentences.zh: 近見卿影《連珠》，寄意悖慢，彌不可長。

translations.literal: Such reports as heard grow worse, clamor in court, not avoiding noble or base, venting words to the extreme, exposing violence to all who hear.
translations.idiomatic: Reports grow worse, clamoring in court, not avoiding rank, speech to the extreme, exposing violence to all who hear.

sentences.zh: 卿不見謝超宗，其才地二三，故在卿前，事殆是百分不一。

translations.literal: Recently seeing your Linked Pearls — intent rebellious and slow, more cannot be borne.
translations.idiomatic: Recently your Linked Pearls — intent rebellious and slow, unbearable.

sentences.zh: 我當原卿性命，令卿萬里思諐。

translations.literal: Have you not seen Xie Chaozong? His talent and standing are two or threefold yours — he stands before you — the affair is perhaps one percent unlike you.
translations.idiomatic: Have you not seen Xie Chaozong? His talent stands two or three ranks above yours — yet his case was perhaps one hundredth unlike yours.

sentences.zh: 卿若能改革，當令卿得還。」

translations.literal: If you can reform, I shall let you return.」
translations.idiomatic: If you can reform, you may return.」

sentences.zh: 獄鞫祥辭。

translations.literal: The prison examined Xiang's words.
translations.idiomatic: The tribunal examined Xiang's defense.

sentences.zh: 祥對曰：「被問『少習狡異，長而不悛，頃來飲酒無度，輕議乘輿，歷貶朝望，每肆醜言，無避尊賤』。

translations.literal: Xiang replied: 「Questioned: from youth learned cunning and strangeness, in age unrepentant; of late drinks without limit, lightly discusses the imperial carriage, deprecates court hope, each time vents ugliness without avoiding noble or base.」
translations.idiomatic: Xiang replied: 「Asked about cunning youth, unrepentant age, drunkenness, slighting the throne, mocking court figures, venting ugliness without regard to rank.」

sentences.zh: 迂答奉旨。

translations.literal: Circuitous answer following the charge.
translations.idiomatic: He answered evasively as ordered.

sentences.zh: 囚出身入官，二十餘年，沈悴草萊，無明天壤。

translations.literal: Your prisoner left coarse cloth and entered office twenty-odd years, sunk in hardship in the grass and fields, without heaven-and-earth's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner entered office twenty-odd years from coarse cloth, sunk in hardship without heaven's clarity.

sentences.zh: 皇運初基，便蒙抽擢，祭酒主簿，竝皆先朝相府。

translations.literal: Your prisoner left coarse cloth and entered office twenty-odd years, sunk in hardship in the grass and fields, without heaven-and-earth's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner entered office twenty-odd years from coarse cloth, sunk in hardship without heaven's clarity.

sentences.zh: 聖明御宇，榮渥彌隆，諮議中郎，一年再澤。

translations.literal: When the imperial fortune first based, he was plucked up — sacrifice officer and chief clerk, all former dynasty's chancellor offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty rose he was plucked up — sacrifice officer and chief clerk in former chancelleries.

sentences.zh: 廣筵華宴，必參末列，朝半問訊，時奉天暉。

translations.literal: The sage brightness rules the realm; glory overflows; adviser and central gentleman — twice favored in one year.
translations.idiomatic: The sage rules; glory overflows; adviser and central gentleman — twice favored in one year.

sentences.zh: 囚雖頑愚，豈不識恩？

translations.literal: Broad mats and splendid feasts — he must join the last row; half the court's inquiries — sometimes he receives heaven's glance.
translations.idiomatic: At broad feasts he sits in the last row; at court inquiries he sometimes receives the throne's glance.

sentences.zh: 有何怨望，敢生譏議？

translations.literal: Your prisoner though dull and foolish — does he not know grace?
translations.idiomatic: Though dull, does your prisoner not know grace?

sentences.zh: 囚歷府以來，伏事四王：武陵功曹，凡涉二載；

translations.literal: What resentment dare he bear to produce mockery?
translations.idiomatic: What resentment dare he bear to mock?

sentences.zh: 長沙諮議，故經少時；

translations.literal: Your prisoner since serving offices has attended four princes: Wuling merit officer, altogether touching two years;
translations.idiomatic: Since serving offices your prisoner attended four princes: Wuling merit officer for two years;

sentences.zh: 奉隷大司馬，竝被恩拂，驃騎中郎，親職少日；

translations.literal: Changsha adviser — therefore only a short time;
translations.idiomatic: Changsha adviser — only a short time;

sentences.zh: 臨川殿下不遺蟲蟻，賜參辭華。

translations.literal: attending the Grand Marshal, all received favor; Rapid Cavalry central gentleman — intimate office few days;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal staff — all favored; Rapid Cavalry attendant — few days in intimate office;

sentences.zh: 司徒殿下文德英明，四海傾屬。

translations.literal: the Prince of Linchuan did not disdain insects and ants and granted him a place among literary flowers.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Linchuan did not disdain him and granted a literary post.

sentences.zh: 囚不涯卑遠，隨例問訊，時節拜覲，亦沾眄議。

translations.literal: The Chancellor's hall's civil virtue bright and clear — the four seas lean toward it.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellor's civil virtue is bright — the realm leans on it.

sentences.zh: 自餘令王，未被祗拜，旣不經伏節，理無厚薄。

translations.literal: Your prisoner did not measure base distance, following precedent inquiring at seasons, at festivals bowing in audience — also gaining sidelong regard.
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner followed precedent at seasonal inquiries and festival audiences — also gaining sidelong notice.

sentences.zh: 敕旨制書，令有疑則啓。

translations.literal: The rest of the princes he has not bowed to — having not received their commands, principle has no thick or thin.
translations.idiomatic: Other princes he has not visited — without their commands there is no obligation thick or thin.

sentences.zh: 囚以天日懸遠，未敢塵穢。

translations.literal: Edicts and regulations order: where there is doubt, memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts order: where there is doubt, memorialize.

sentences.zh: 私之疑事，衞將軍臣儉，宰輔聖朝，令望當世，囚自斷才短，密以諮儉，儉爲折衷，紙迹猶存。

translations.literal: Your prisoner because heaven's sun hangs far did not dare defile; private doubtful matters — Defender General Wang Jian, chief minister of the holy reign, fame fit for the age — your prisoner judged his talent short and secretly consulted Jian; Jian made the compromise — paper traces still exist.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's sun hangs far — your prisoner did not dare defile; private doubts he secretly consulted Wang Jian — Jian compromised; the paper still exists.

sentences.zh: 未解此理云何敢爲『歷貶朝望』。

translations.literal: Not understanding this principle — how dare he 「deprecate court hope」?
translations.idiomatic: Not understanding this — how dare he 「mock court figures」?

sentences.zh: 云囚『輕議乘輿』，爲向誰道？

translations.literal: Saying your prisoner 「lightly discusses the imperial carriage」 — to whom did he speak?
translations.idiomatic: 「Slighting the throne」 — to whom did he speak?

sentences.zh: 若向人道，則應有主甲，豈有事無髣彿，空見羅謗？

translations.literal: If he spoke to others there should be a chief accuser; how can matters be without likeness, empty slander alone?
translations.idiomatic: If to others there should be an accuser; how can empty slander stand without likeness?

sentences.zh: 囚性不耐酒，親知所悉，強進一升，便已迷醉。

translations.literal: Your prisoner's nature cannot bear wine — close kin know it; forced to one sheng he is already drunk.」
translations.idiomatic: Your prisoner cannot bear wine — kin know it; one cup and he is drunk.」

sentences.zh: 」其餘事事自申。

translations.literal: The rest he answered item by item.
translations.idiomatic: The rest he answered item by item.

sentences.zh: 乃徙廣州。

translations.literal: He was then exiled to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祥至廣州，不得意，終日縱酒，少時病卒，年三十九。

translations.literal: Xiang reaching Guangzhou was discontent, drank all day, and soon died of illness, aged thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Guangzhou he was discontent, drank all day, and soon died of illness at thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 祥從祖兄彪，祥曾祖穆之正胤。

translations.literal: Xiang's agnatic elder Biao — Xiang's great-grandfather Muzhi's legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang's agnatic cousin Biao was legitimate heir of great-grandfather Muzhi.

sentences.zh: 建元初，降封南康縣公，虎賁中郎將。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyuan he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Nankang, tiger-guard central gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianyuan's start he was demoted to Duke of Nankang, tiger-guard central gentleman.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，坐廟墓不脩削爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming he was reduced in rank for not repairing the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year one he lost rank for not repairing the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 後爲羽林監。

translations.literal: Later he was feathered-forest supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was feathered-forest supervisor.

sentences.zh: 九年，又坐與亡弟母楊別居，不相料理，楊死不殯葬，崇聖寺尼慧首剃頭爲尼，以五百錢爲買棺材，以泥洹轝送葬劉墓。

translations.literal: In year nine he was again charged with living separately from his dead younger brother's mother Yang without managing her; when Yang died he did not bury her — Chong Sheng Temple nun Huishou shaved her head as a nun; with five hundred cash bought a coffin; with a clay-wheeled hearse sent burial to the Liu tomb.
translations.idiomatic: In year nine he was charged with living apart from his dead brother's mother Yang and not caring for her; when Yang died he did not bury her — a nun bought a coffin for five hundred cash and sent burial to the Liu tomb.

sentences.zh: 爲有司所奏，事寢不出。

translations.literal: The relevant office memorialized; the affair was shelved and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: Offices memorialized; the affair was shelved.

sentences.zh: 【評贊】

translations.literal: Comment and eulogy
translations.idiomatic: Comment and eulogy

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：魏文帝云「文人不護細行」，古今之所同也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Wei Emperor Wen said 「literary men do not guard small conduct」 — ancient and modern are the same.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Cao Pi said 「literary men do not guard small conduct」 — ancient and modern agree.

sentences.zh: 由自知情深，在物無競，身名之外，一概可蔑。

translations.literal: Because they know feeling is deep, in things they do not compete; beyond body and name — all may be scorned.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their feeling runs deep, they do not compete in things; beyond body and name — all may be scorned.

sentences.zh: 旣徇斯道，其弊彌流，聲裁所加，取忤人世。

translations.literal: Having followed this Way, the harm flows wider; what sound and judgment add takes offense at the worldly.
translations.idiomatic: Following this Way, harm flows wider; reputation takes offense at the world.

sentences.zh: 向之所以貴身，翻成害己。

translations.literal: What once made the body honored turns to harm oneself.
translations.idiomatic: What once honored the body turns to harm oneself.

sentences.zh: 故通人立訓，爲之而不恃也。

translations.literal: Therefore the penetrating man sets instruction and acts yet does not rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the wise set instruction and act without relying on it.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：超宗蘊文，祖構餘芬。

translations.literal: Eulogy: Chaozong stored literature, ancestors' lingering fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Chaozong held literature, ancestral fragrance lingering.

sentences.zh: 劉祥慕異，言亦不羣。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang admired the strange; his words too stood apart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang admired strangeness; his words stood apart.

sentences.zh: 違朝失典，流放南濆。

translations.literal: Violating court and losing canon, exiled to the southern shore.
translations.idiomatic: Violating court and losing canon, exiled to the southern shore.
